text:
incident-bot: 🔔 Paging oncall — P2: Dedicated pool cache hit-rate collapse for tenant=tenant-acme-42 in us-west-2 dedicated pool. Symptoms: spike in latency, increased token costs, and elevated 5xx rates for requests pinned to acme's models. Notifying oncall and eng-ml.

Alice Tran: I'm on it. Seeing customer-facing errors reported via support channel. Can someone paste the cache metrics?

Ben Ruiz: attaching quick numbers from observability — hit_rate dropped from ~0.86 to ~0.05 over ~12m, eviction rate spiked.

Cheng Li: logs show a huge number of unique prefixes from that tenant (cardinality explosion). Likely cache pollution — many ephemeral keys with high churn.

Evan Scully: Confirmed on our side: dedicated pool "dedicated-usw2-acme" CPU and GPU not saturated, but per-tenant cache performance tanked. Routing still to same pool, causing request latency to climb.

Alice Tran: TLDR: cache hit-rate collapse for tenant-acme -> latency + cost. Immediate mitigations?

Cheng Li: Recommend: 1) disable prefix/KV cache for tenant-acme temporarily; 2) flush tenant-specific cache namespaces; 3) route traffic to fallback variant ("no-cache") for canary; 4) add temporary per-tenant cache admission limit.

Ben Ruiz: I'm executing the disable and flush now. Will update when done.

Ben Ruiz: (command)
```
# disable prefix cache for tenant-acme-42
redwoodctl cache set --tenant tenant-acme-42 --policy disabled
# flush tenant prefix namespace
redwoodctl cache flush --tenant tenant-acme-42 --prefix "kv/" --force
```

Ben Ruiz: done. API returned 200 for both calls. Confirming propagation to all nodes.

oncall-ml: Running quick sanity checks for correctness/regression risk. Disabling cache will increase token costs but should restore latency stability. Recommend rolling to fallback "no-cache" model variant for 5% of traffic first.

Alice Tran: @Dana Ortiz please let ACME account team know we are taking these mitigations (disable cache + flush). They'll need to expect a temporary performance/cost blip.

Dana Ortiz: pinged Acme SE (Frank) and account team. Frank: we're disabling your tenant cache to protect traffic. Any immediate concerns we should surface to customer?

Frank (Acme SE): Thanks — customer has some real-time session keys but no committed SLAs on cache behavior. They prefer us to proceed. Please keep logs of requests that fail so we can correlate.

Cheng Li: Observability snippets (after disable + flush):
```
[2026-03-14T16:12:05Z] tenant=tenant-acme-42 cache_hits=12 cache_requests=240 hit_rate=0.05 evictions=13452
[2026-03-14T16:23:10Z] tenant=tenant-acme-42 cache_hits=2 cache_requests=250 hit_rate=0.008 evictions=14001
[2026-03-14T16:28:40Z] cache policy applied -> disabled for tenant-acme-42
```

Evan Scully: After flush, we're seeing latency stabilize on p50/p95. Token costs look higher ~+18% for acme traffic (as oncall-ml warned) but CPU/GPU utilization OK.

Alice Tran: Good. Next: we need to identify root cause — why so many unique keys? Cheng, can you pull sample offending prefixes?

Cheng Li: Sample keys (high cardinality patterns):
- `session:random-<uuid>` repeated once per request
- `ctx:user:<user_id>:ts:<unix_ms>` short TTLs but unique per message
- `acme:temp:key:<ephemeral>`
Looks like the app is using the KV/prefix cache as a per-request store, causing pollution.

Ben Ruiz: Also saw a recent deploy on acme side (UserService) at ~2026-03-14T15:55 that changed session key generation. Could be correlated.

Dana Ortiz: I've scheduled a call with Acme engineering for 18:00 PT to discuss longer-term mitigations. They want us to restore cache once we can guarantee admission controls.

oncall-ml: Proposed longer-term fixes:
- Per-tenant cache quota (hard cap on unique keys)
- Admission policy: deny caching for keys matching high-cardinality regexes (e.g., containing timestamps/uuids)
- Default TTL floor and max-entries per-tenant
- Alerting on sudden drop in hit_rate and eviction spikes

Alice Tran: Agree. Immediate post-incident tasks:
1) Keep cache disabled for tenant-acme until after product/SE sync.
2) Add a temporary rate limit on key creation in routing layer to slow the pollution.
3) Create an incident ticket and postmortem stub.
4) Add runbook step: how to flush and disable per-tenant cache (commands).

Ben Ruiz: Creating incident ticket now and adding logs + timeline. Ticket ID: INC-2026-1442.

Cheng Li: I'll prototype an admission rule (reject keys matching `/[0-9]{13}/` or long UUIDs) and test in staging. If that looks good, we can roll to dedicated-usw2-acme next week behind a feature flag.

Evan Scully: Ops note: we applied a temporary route override to send 100% acme traffic to a separate dedicated-backup pool to minimize blast radius while the cache is disabled. Command used: `redwoodctl route set --tenant tenant-acme-42 --pool dedicated-usw2-backup --force`. Verified connection.

Dana Ortiz: Customer update posted to #acme-support: "We have isolated the issue to tenant-specific cache pollution. We disabled tenant cache and flushed keys. Your traffic is routed to backup pool. Engineering will follow up with remediation plan." They replied :thumbsup:.

Frank (Acme SE): Please keep detailed metrics for their finance team — the cost bump needs to be documented. They asked for ETA for re-enabling cache after admission rules; said they'd prefer a soft roll.

Alice Tran: Plan for next 24h:
- Keep cache disabled and routing override in place (Ben/Evan)
- Cheng to land admission-rule prototype in staging and run synthetic canary (Cheng/oncall-ml)
- Dana/Frank handle customer comms and cost breakdown (Dana/Ben)
- Postmortem scheduled and runbook updated (Ben/Alice)

oncall-ml: Logging suggestion: capture top-100 prefixes by key cardinality per tenant for 48h (non-PII), store in object store for postmortem. I'll add a short pipeline to do this.

Ben Ruiz: Noted. Also adding alert: if tenant_hit_rate < 0.2 AND evictions > 1k in 10m -> auto-disable cache for that tenant (experimental).

Alice Tran: If there are no objections, I'll escalate to reliability meeting tomorrow for long-term design: per-tenant quotas, admission, better defaults.

Cheng Li: I'll post a short RFC once I have the staging results.

Evan Scully: Closing loop: latencies are stable and 5xxs decreased after mitigations. Keeping thread open until we re-enable cache behind admission controls.

Dana Ortiz: Customer confirmed they're fine with the approach. We'll coordinate re-enable once Cheng has a tested policy.

Ben Ruiz: Incident ticket INC-2026-1442 updated and assigned. Files attached: logs, sample keys, graph snapshots.

Alice Tran: Great work everyone. Moving to monitoring phase — leave thread comments for progress updates. Will run full postmortem after re-enable. :white_check_mark:
